approach.method_basis: The reference is Augmented Hill-Climb, a molecule generator that writes SMILES one token at a time, like a small language model, and is nudged toward the objective by rewriting its own probabilities. First a prior is trained on an unlabeled corpus of molecules, learning only what valid chemistry looks like and nothing about any objective. For each objective a fresh copy of that prior becomes the policy, while the original stays frozen as a reference. After each batch of molecules comes back scored, only the best-scoring half is kept, and the policy is pushed so that the log-likelihood it assigns to each of those elite sequences moves toward a fixed target: the frozen prior's log-likelihood for the same molecule plus a constant times the observed reward. That target is what makes it a hill-climb rather than a policy gradient - the update is a squared regression onto an explicit number, so a molecule that scored well becomes proportionally more likely to be written again while the frozen prior keeps the policy anchored to real chemistry. New candidates are then sampled directly from the updated policy, canonicalised, and any invalid or repeated ones replaced by sampling more. Low-scoring molecules contribute nothing to the update at all.
approach.novelty: The method statement leaves the update's aggressiveness, its scope and its recovery behaviour open, and this implementation pins all three down. Elites are the top-scoring half of each batch, five of ten, with at least one always retained, so the update never sees an empty training set. The reward multiplier is fixed at sixty and each update is twelve clipped-gradient steps, which is a deliberately sharp commitment: the fixed regression target moves the elite likelihood a long way per batch rather than nudging it. Scope is strictly the batch just scored - no historical replay, no randomized SMILES augmentation, no reuse of earlier elites - so the policy is always chasing its most recent feedback and the root deliberately declines the replay variants that the same method family usually adds. The molecules supplied at initialization are treated as the first scored batch, so the policy is already adapted before it emits anything. Invalid or already-seen samples are replaced by continued sampling from the same policy rather than any fallback, and the exact token sequence that produced each submitted structure is stored and reused for training, so the likelihood being raised belongs to the molecule that was actually scored.

observed_bottleneck: This is an unevaluated lineage root and the supplied campaign evidence is empty. The benchmark difficulty is making a de novo molecular language generator respond to sparse objective feedback quickly enough to discover a strong final molecule. An unlabeled language prior supplies valid chemistry but no task-specific preference, while updates using every low-reward sample can dilute the limited favorable feedback.
hypothesis: A corpus-trained autoregressive SMILES policy is adapted independently in each objective by Augmented Hill-Climb on only the current scored batch elites, fitting policy log likelihood toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward, and proposes new molecules by direct token sampling from the updated policy.

finding_summary.headline: Elite-only likelihood sharpening saturates one objective completely and collapses on another, placing fifth of thirteen roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a sharp picture of when elite likelihood sharpening pays. Among the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits fifth at 0.4766, but the aggregate hides the real signal: this method produced both the strongest single-objective result in this group and the weakest. Where a learnable structural motif exists and is reachable from the corpus prior, sharpening onto it is extremely effective - one objective is essentially solved. Where the reward distribution collapses, it has nothing to work with: on the weakest objective the median score across the entire run was exactly zero, its mean elite squared error was 4.94 against 735 on the objective that saturated, and the only two updates in the whole node that increased loss were both from that run. An elite half selected from ten molecules that all score zero is an arbitrary five, and the policy then drifts back to generic prior chemistry. That is a concrete, actionable characterisation of the method's failure mode and a strong argument that any Development on this lineage should target the low-signal regime - a reward transform, a ranking that survives ties, or the historical replay the root deliberately declined - rather than the update rule itself. A second caution: elite likelihood rose in only 111 of 150 individual updates even though the aggregate is clearly positive, so single updates are noisy and the mechanism works on average rather than reliably. Still open: one seed, no paired comparison, no anchor decision, and no evidence on whether the drd2_docking saturation reflects a genuinely easy objective or a policy exploiting it.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.4766 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.6029 on deco_hop, 0.99999961 on drd2_docking, 0.1844 on median_2, 0.1428 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4532 on zaleplon_mpo. That drd2_docking figure is effectively a saturated objective and the highest single-task result among the three roots examined here; the sitagliptin_mpo figure is the lowest. All observables behaved as intended and the falsifier was not triggered. The corpus prior learned well - token-normalized next-token loss fell from 4.5609 to 0.5625 on a fixed 4096-sequence holdout over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences - and was verifiably frozen thereafter, with the prior checkpoint hash and zero prior-parameter changes recorded across all 5 initializations and all 150 updates. The update mechanism did what it claims: mean elite squared error fell from 201.89 to 110.54, decreasing in 148 of 150 updates, and mean elite sequence log-likelihood rose by +2.321 while non-elite log-likelihood fell by -1.052, confirming the update is genuinely selective rather than raising everything. All 750 training members were verified to be the current batch's top-scoring half, with zero historical replay anywhere. Generation stayed healthy: 10492 of 11632 sampled sequences were RDKit-valid, a rate of 0.902, and all 145 rounds filled a batch of exactly ten valid novel molecules with zero rejections at the evaluator.

molecular.headline: The most conventionally drug-like molecules of the three roots, converging hard onto one clean series per run when the reward has signal
molecular.overall_character: This generator writes real medicinal chemistry. Ring-closure rate is 0.983 to 0.997 and aromatic-atom rate 0.948 to 0.997 in every run, cumulated double bonds are essentially absent at 0.000 in four runs and 0.003 in the fifth, and molecules are compact, with mean SMILES lengths of 36.0, 36.7, 37.4, 42.6 and 57.9. The unstable-motif tail that the other roots in this trio produce - peroxides, hypervalent sulfur, strained C=N-O rings, allenes - is largely absent here, because the corpus language prior anchors every sample to chemistry it has actually seen. The characteristic behaviour is convergence: in each run where the reward carried information, the twelve best molecules are one clean series permuted by substituent, exactly the mode collapse an elite-only likelihood update should produce. Two systematic limits remain. Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs, so a series built entirely on a substituted saturated ring is emitted with no configuration at all. And where the reward is degenerate the convergence simply does not happen and the output reverts to unrelated commodity structures from the prior - long alkylamines, alkyl phosphonates, tiny saturated heterocycles - alongside the useful chemistry. One run also shows the generator learning to pile on cheap score-raising decoration, reaching a halogen rate of 0.824 and a charged rate of 0.228 in polyfluorinated, nitro-bearing, N-oxide chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: Clean, small, almost entirely aromatic amides: indole and azaindole 2-carboxamides coupled to tetrahydroisoquinoline or isoindoline, plus a family of anthranilamide-aminopyridines. Mean SMILES length is 36.7 and halogen rate only 0.155, so the run built its score from ring and amide chemistry rather than from decoration.
liabilities: Nitro-substituted heteroaromatics recurring in the zero-scoring tail
A quaternary phosphocholine-like surfactant sampled straight from the prior
Oversized multi-aryl condensation products in the tail that consume oracle calls
missing_features: No fluorinated aniline of the kind present in the best supplied starting molecule
No stereochemistry anywhere in the run
No saturated three-dimensional core - almost every winner is flat
No basic amine side chain on the winning series
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 0.453 winner is an anthranilamide with an aminopyridine, and the eleven behind it are a single indole-2-carboxamide-tetrahydroisoquinoline series permuted by methyl, ethyl, ethoxy, methoxy and ring-nitrogen position, spanning 0.380 to 0.443. Replacing the amide with a sulfonamide on the same skeleton drops the score from 0.453 to 0.380 and then to 0.246, so the carbonyl is doing real work and the policy found that and then explored around it.

per_task.generated_character: A tetrafluorinated biaryl carbohydrazide series decorated with nitro groups, pyridine N-oxides and trifluoromethyl. Halogen rate reaches 0.824 and charged rate 0.228, both by a wide margin the highest anywhere in this node, and the aromatic rate is 0.997 - almost every heavy atom is in an aromatic ring.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones throughout the winning series, a reactive and metabolically labile motif
Multiple nitro groups combined with pyridine N-oxides on the same molecule
Perfluorinated aromatic rings that would be far outside ordinary lead-like property space
missing_features: No purinedione or fused bicyclic imide core from the starting molecules
No saturated linkers, and no stereochemistry on anything sp3
No basic ionizable nitrogen to balance the electron-poor rings
No structural alternative to the acylhydrazone once it was found
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All twelve best sit within 0.586 to 0.603 and share the same acylhydrazone-tetrafluorobiaryl skeleton, differing only in which electron-poor group decorates which ring. The losing tail is plain unfunctionalised aromatics - diphenylmethane, coumaric acid, a diarylmethanol - sitting at the 0.500 floor that trivial structures occupy. So the gradient rewards piling electron-withdrawing decoration onto a fixed skeleton, and the policy learned exactly that.

per_task.generated_character: A textbook arylalkylamine series: 3-aryl piperidines and ring-expanded azepanes, N-alkylated with propyl or butyl, paired with a chloro- and fluoro-substituted phenethylamine or a strained azetidine amine. Mean SMILES length is 36.0, the shortest of the five runs, and these are the most conventionally drug-like molecules anywhere in the three roots examined.
liabilities: Strained azetidine amines used as primary-amine bioisosteres throughout the top
Ring-expanded azepanes and azocanes of doubtful synthetic accessibility
Alkyl fluoride chains attached to the ring nitrogen, which would be metabolically labile
missing_features: No stereochemistry on the 3-aryl saturated ring centre, which is where the real pharmacology of this series sits
No scaffold alternatives explored once the series was found
No polar or solubilising substituents anywhere on the saturated ring
No aromatic ring systems beyond a single substituted benzene
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Eleven of the top twelve score at least 0.99999 and every one of them carries the same pair: an N-alkyl saturated cyclic amine and a second basic nitrogen on a halogenated aromatic. The tail at 4e-05 to 4e-04 keeps aromatic amides, nitro groups and ureas but has no basic aliphatic nitrogen at all, so the objective has a hard structural switch. The run was effectively saturated by round 28 and the remaining budget went into permuting alkyl chain length and halogen position on an already-solved series.

per_task.generated_character: Aryl sulfonamides and piperazine or tetrahydroisoquinoline amides - ordinary lead-like medicinal chemistry with mean SMILES length 37.4, no cumulated bonds and no obviously unstable motifs. A sulfonyl-tetrahydroisoquinoline motif recurs across the top but does not dominate it the way the winning series does in the other runs.
liabilities: A sulfoxonium-like charged sulfur group appearing in the final batch
An unbranched C18 alkylamine sampled directly from the prior and submitted
An alkyl phosphonate diester with no relevance to the chemistry being searched
missing_features: No fused aminal cage of the kind this objective's strongest chemistry uses
No stereochemistry on the sp3 ring centres produced
No convergence onto a single elaborated series across 29 rounds
No electron-rich alkoxy-substituted biaryl arms
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top twelve span 0.161 to 0.184 and are only loosely related, while the 0.014 to 0.040 tail is long-chain aliphatics, an alkyl phosphonate, a tiny imidazoline and a saturated terpenoid. So the gradient rewards aromatic sulfonamide content over aliphatic bulk but is shallow throughout, and the run never found a step large enough for the elite update to lock onto - the final batch scores 0.099 to 0.139, below the top twelve.

per_task.generated_character: Generic prior chemistry that never organised into anything: phthalimides, benzylamines, triazole acetamides, aryl sulfonamides and oxadiazoles, all unrelated to one another. The molecules are individually plausible - ring rate 0.983, aromatic rate 0.948, no cumulated bonds - but there is no series here at all, which is the visible signature of an update with no reward signal to sharpen.
liabilities: Long dialkylamino thiol chains sampled from the prior in the zero-scoring tail
Azo linkages between aromatic rings paired with bis-cationic quinolinium centres
Acyclic diester and diacid chains with no relation to the objective
missing_features: No trifluoromethyl-substituted aromatic ring on the winning molecules
No beta-amino amide or fused triazolopyrazine motif
No stereochemistry, although the chemistry this objective rewards is stereodefined
No compact saturated fluorinated heterocycle
No convergence of any kind across 29 rounds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The median score across the entire run is exactly zero and the best is 0.143. Only three molecules clear 0.10 and the twelfth-best is already at 0.031, so the elite half of a typical batch is five molecules that all scored zero and carry no ordering. The final batch scores 0.0, 0.004, 0.0, 0.0004, 0.0 and 0.00003, and those six molecules share nothing structurally with the top of the run - the policy had drifted back to prior-typical output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the three runs where the reward carried information, the twelve best molecules share a complete skeleton and differ only in alkyl chain length, halogen identity or ring-nitrogen position. In one of them eleven of the top twelve exceed 0.99999 on the same series, and the last rounds of the budget were spent permuting decoration on chemistry that was already saturated.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator collapses to one skeleton and then only permutes substituents on it
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Raising the likelihood of elite sequences directly narrows the sampling distribution, so once a series is found the generator can no longer reach anything else. A generator needs a diversity term, a likelihood ceiling per motif, or periodic resampling from the unadapted prior, so that budget remaining after a series is exhausted is spent on a different region rather than on redundant analogues.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the run whose median score across all 290 evaluations was exactly zero, mean elite squared error was 4.94 against 735 in the run that converged, the only two loss-increasing updates in the whole node came from it, and its final six molecules scored at or near zero while sharing no structure with its own best. That run also shows no series at all, in contrast to every run that had signal.
transferable_gaps.gap: A degenerate reward distribution leaves the update with nothing to learn from
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Selecting the top-scoring half is meaningless when the whole batch scores the same, so the elite set becomes an arbitrary sample and the update pushes the policy toward noise. A generator that adapts from feedback needs a signal that survives ties - a ranking over the whole history, a reward transform that spreads a collapsed distribution, or a fallback to pure exploration when within-batch variance vanishes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five independent runs across 1450 molecules, including a run whose entire winning series is built on a substituted saturated ring carbon where configuration determines the chemistry, and another whose target chemistry is explicitly stereodefined.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry is ever produced, including on series that are defined by it
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The token vocabulary and the sampling procedure produce flat connectivity only, so the model cannot express, learn or sharpen configuration even when the feedback rewards it. A generator needs stereochemical tokens present in the prior's training data and preserved through canonicalisation, so that two configurations of a skeleton are distinguishable candidates rather than the same string.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one run the generator drove the halogen rate to 0.824 and the charged rate to 0.228, converging on perfluorinated biaryls carrying nitro groups and pyridine N-oxides, with all twelve best within 0.017 of each other. It found that adding electron-poor substituents to a fixed skeleton moved the score and kept doing so rather than changing the skeleton.
transferable_gaps.gap: Cheap decoration is exploited in place of structural change
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A likelihood update rewards whatever raises the number, and substituent decoration is the cheapest available move because it changes few tokens. A generator would need property-space constraints applied to its own output distribution, so that a mode built entirely from extreme decoration is penalised before it consumes the remaining budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 11632 sampled sequences, 1140 failed to parse, a validity rate of 0.902, and 4781 further proposals were rejected as duplicates or invalid during refill. Among the structures that did pass, the low-scoring tails contain unbranched C18 alkylamines, alkyl phosphonate diesters, a phosphocholine surfactant and bare four-atom heterocycles - prior-typical output with no relevance to any search.
transferable_gaps.gap: Around a tenth of what the generator writes is not a molecule, and some of what is remains commodity chemistry
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Sampling ancestrally from a language model has no mechanism to keep drawn sequences inside a useful region of chemistry, so budget goes to parsing failures and to generic corpus material. A generator needs constrained decoding that guarantees a parseable structure, plus a property or complexity filter applied before submission, so that invalid and trivially irrelevant draws are replaced without paying for them.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
